articles.title: ‘We’ll hear them out’: Sydney Swans prepare for banned players’ return to club
articles.summary: Heeney, Warner, Blakey, Jordon and Bice set for exit meetings. The five will ‘have a chat to the broader group and the club’ Sydney’s five suspended players are set to make their return and will address the Swans’ playing group “at some point”.
body: Swans coach Dean Cox confirmed to reporters Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice will return to headquarters for the usual end-of-season exit meetings from Wednesday.
Cox arrived at the club’s Moore Park base early on Wednesday morning, before Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich briefly spoke to media.

“Look, it’s a natural thing that the players will come into the club over the next period,” Pavlich said. “Don’t know exactly when that’ll be, given that the season’s now finished and player exit meetings are occurring.
“And the players at some point will have a chat to the broader group and the club, but yeah, there’s no timeline.”

articles.title: Mariona Caldentey penalty provides late WCL relief for Arsenal against Køge
articles.summary: Mariona Caldentey’s 93rd-minute penalty delivered a win and a hefty dose of relief to fans bouncing behind the goal in the North Bank after the ball hit the back of the net, but ­Arsenal’s narrow defeat of HB Køge in their Champions League opener left more questions unanswered than answered for the…
body: The puffed cheeks of the manager, Renée Slegers, said it all when the full-time whistle went. If it had been revealed after the final whistle that a force field surrounded the opposition goal at Meadow Park, many would have believed it, such was the extent of Arsenal’s ridiculous profligacy in front of goal in their league-phase opener.
“It was a mentality and resilience win today,” said Slegers. “The football didn’t give us the win … but we get the goal as a squad.”
Exactly what is stopping Arsenal from getting the ball in the back of the net with a swagger reflective of their talent-laden squad is hard to pinpoint.

Yes, teams are defending excellently against them, as a battling Køge and their goalkeeper Alberte Vingum did on Tuesday night, but this feels like an Arsenal problem: a mentality one, a training ground one, a ruthlessness one.

articles.title: Giants’ Jaxson Dart could reportedly miss rest of season with knee injury
articles.summary: Testing said to reveal injury is worse than anticipated. Quarterback was hurt against Rams on Monday. New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will be out for an extended period of time and could miss the rest of the NFL season after suffering a knee injury in Monday night’s loss to the Los Angeles…
body: ESPN reported that the injury to Dart’s left knee was more severe than initially anticipated. Adam Schefter said further testing has left the Giants and Dart facing the possibility of season-ending surgery.

The second-year quarterback was hurt on the opening possession of the Giants’ 28-6 defeat to the Rams. Initial reports said that Dart sprained his MCL and avoided broken bones, with an MRI set for Tuesday. Head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that he believed a “devastating outcome” had been avoided and that he did not expect Dart to be out long-term without giving a further recovery timeline.

The 23-year-old started the season strong in New York’s Week 1 win over Dallas but left the field after taking a huge hit from Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart on the Giants’ seventh play Monday night. Dart watched the second half in a track suit on the sidelines. Jameis Winston could not get much going after Dart’s exit, throwing an end-zone interception as New York got all of their points from field goals.

articles.title: Will anyone topple Infantino? How Fifa president is trying to cling on after World Cup sell-off debacle
articles.summary: Fifa president continues to lobby for re-election despite no other candidates coming forward to challenge him. For Gianni Infantino there is no international break. The Fifa president is widely expected to make an appearance at the United Nations general assembly this week in New York, where he…
body: Infantino has not been idle during the lull since Fifa abandoned its World Cup sell-off plan last month, instead crisscrossing the globe on a private jet provided by Qatar Airways as part of its sponsorship deal with world football’s governing body.

From his strongholds in Doha, Rabat and Miami, Infantino has also visited Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Kyrgyzstan and various other countries, his trips often coinciding with the approval of funding for development projects worth millions of dollars. His would-be opponents have been conspicuous by their silence.

Whether Qatar Airways facilitating Infantino’s re-election campaign should be considered legitimate Fifa presidential business is a moot point, which neatly encapsulates the huge incumbency bias that will benefit Infantino if a vote takes place at the Fifa congress in March. That ballot appears to be in doubt, with multiple sources involved in the push to remove Infantino telling the Guardian they are running out of hope of finding a candidate to beat him.

articles.title: Hawks Must Execute One Big Trade Before Window Closes
articles.summary: The Atlanta Hawks sit right on the edge of something special. They have the pieces to win now, but they are missing one specific type of player to get over the hump. According to Soaring Down South, the team is still just one big swing trade away from becoming a legitimate contender in the East.
body: That missing piece is a star who can create offense on the outside. The current roster has talent, but it lacks a true lead creator who can take over a game when the defense tightens up. The team needs a guy who can handle the ball and threaten from deep or in the mid-range to open things up for everyone else.

Many fans might not realize how good the foundation actually is. Jalen Johnson has already arrived as an All-Star, which changes the entire dynamic of the offense. He is the engine, but he needs help. Soaring Down South reports that the Hawks currently lack a perimeter star of sufficient quality to partner with him.

The supporting cast is actually quite deep and versatile. Dyson Daniels brings elite defense to the floor, making life hard for opposing guards. Nickeil Alexander-Walker acts as a great secondary shock creator who can get buckets when needed. Onyeka Okongwu is a quality starting center who protects the rim. These players give the team a solid base to build upon.
points: The Atlanta Hawks sit right on the edge of something special.
They have the pieces to win now, but they are missing one specific type of player to get over the hump.

articles.title: GB boxers guaranteed three medals at Europeans
articles.summary: Britain guarantee at least three medals at the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria as Chantelle Reid, Damar Thomas and Abdul Burton all reach the semi-finals.
body: Great Britain are guaranteed at least three medals at the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria after Chantelle Reid, Damar Thomas and Abdul Burton reached the semi-finals.
Reid cruised to a 5-0 win over Ireland's Evelyn Igharo in a women's light-middleweight contest at the Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia.
The 28-year-old Commonwealth Games silver medallist will face Serbia's Milena Matovic in the last four on Wednesday.
Thomas won by the same margin in a men's super-heavyweight fight against Georgia's Nikoloz Begadze and the 21-year-old will take on Mahammad Abdullayev of Azerbaijan in the semi-finals.

articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians moved closer to clinching an American League playoff spot, beating the Boston Red Sox 3-2 on Tuesday, Sept. 22. Nathaniel Lowe's sacrifice fly scored Chase DeLauter with the winning run in the top of the ninth.
body: Guardians closer Cade Smith worked a scoreless ninth to earn his 40th save.
Cleveland lowered its magic number to clinching a playoff spot to two and will remain atop the AL Central Division.
Parker Messick delivered a solid start for the Guardians, leaving with a one-run lead and shot at his 13th win of the season.

Cleveland scored its first two runs in the second, taking a 2-0 lead. David Fry 's RBI single brought home Angel Martinez with the first run. Martinez had a three-hit game. Fry later scored the second run when Brayan Rocchio grounded into a double play.

articles.title: Snedeker wants Spaun to 'make me look like an idiot' after Presidents Cup snub
articles.summary: Brandt Snedeker said he wants JJ Spaun "to make me look like an idiot" after leaving the former US Open champion out of his Presidents Cup side.
body: Spaun became just the third American to win the BMW PGA Championship, joining Arnold Palmer and Billy Horschel, and the first player to claim the title on their debut since Byeong-hun An in 2015.

The 36-year-old was controversially overlooked by Snedeker for a place in his side to face the International Team in the biennial match-play event, which pits the best golfers from the United States against the top international players at Medinah Country Club and is live from Thursday on Sky Sports.
Spaun admitted he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" at Wentworth, saying he had a point to prove and that missing out on the Presidents Cup had added fuel to his fire.

"Being a captain, you have to make tough decisions, unfortunately, and we had 15 or 16 guys that we were really looking at," said Snedeker, who also named Ryan Gerard, Akshay Bhatia and Gary Woodland - a US team vice-captain at this year's Presidents Cup - as close calls during his deliberations over the captain's picks.

articles.summary: Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors will be subject to an independent investigation into their conduct and actions over the past 12 months, the Rugby Football League (RFL) has said.
body: The Leopards and the Warriors have had an ongoing dispute for almost 12 months, dating back to the high-profile ticketing saga that led to Leigh's owner Derek Beaumont saying his club would not participate in the fixture over a disagreement about their ticket allocation of 4,800.
They ultimately did play the game and were eliminated from the play-offs with Wigan winning 18-6.

With the Warriors set to host Wakefield in the play-off semi-final on Saturday, matters reignited again over the weekend after an original post from Wigan detailed ticketing arrangements for whichever side visited the Brick this weekend in the play-offs would receive an allocation of 5,000 tickets for safety reasons.
Leigh were beaten by Wakefield Trinity in their eliminator match, where a win for the Leopards would have seen them progress to face Wigan instead.
